news.title: Football: Soccer-FIFA suspends coach Hassan and forward Zico for three and five matches
news.lede: Oct 19 (Reuters) - FIFA has ⁠suspended Egypt coach Hossam Hassan and forward Mostafa Zico ⁠for three and five matches respectively, the Egyptian Football ‌Association said on Monday, after theycriticisedthe referee following a 3-2 defeat by Argentina in the World Cup. The 60-year-old Hassan was sanctioned after blaming refereeing errors ​for his country's elimination from the ⁠tournament in the last 16, ⁠whileZico insulted the referee in a post-match interview. Ibrahim Hassan, Hossam's twin ⁠brother ‌and Egypt's national team director, has also been suspended for three matches. "The decisions include the suspension of ⁠Hossam Hassan and Ibrahim Hassan for three matches ​each, while Zico ‌has been suspended for five matches," the EFA said ⁠in a ​statement.

news.title: Uefa demands Fifa releases documents relating to World Cup sell-off scheme
news.lede: European governing body gives two-week deadline. Letter addresses other issues including Balogun affair. Uefa has given Fifa a two-week deadline to release key documents relating to Gianni Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan and other governance issues in its latest critique of football’s world governing body. A letter sent to Fifa’s general secretary, Mattias Grafström, by his counterpart at Uefa, Theodore Theodoridis, is accompanied by an eight-page document that has more than 50 questions about Fifa’s handling of dozens of issues over the past 12 months.

news.title: Junior Starlets 2026 World Cup campaign off to a sour start with defeat to China
news.lede: Kenya’s Junior Starlets got their 2026 FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup campaign off on the wrong foot after suffering a 3-0 Group E opening defeat to China PR on Monday evening at the Mohammed VI Football Academy in Rabat, Morocco. The Junior Starlets are making their second-ever World Cup appearance after making history in 2024. They were hoping for a brighter start this time around and to progress beyond the group-stage exit they experienced back then, where they managed just one win in the Dominican Republic. However, China, making their fifth appearance on the global stage, proved too strong and capitalised on defensive frailties to get their campaign off to a flying start.

news.title: Trump at centre of Infantino World Cup sell-off plot as UEFA poses 42 questions
news.lede: European football bosses have demanded answers about Gianni Infantino's alleged "conflicts of interest" over business dealings with the Trump family and the World Cup sell-off attempt. In the letter, obtained by Sky News , UEFA includes a list of 42 questions to FIFA after Mr Infantino had a meeting of the world football's council last week. UEFA writes: "A series of decisions, transactions and interventions involving the FIFA President, the President of the United States and individuals associated with him raise serious questions concerning potential conflicts of interest, transparency and institutional accountability." It suggests there are concerns about Mr Infantino's discussions with Donald Trump and associates over the creation of a FIFA cryptocurrency, which was reported by Sky News in February.

news.title: U-17 Women’s World Cup: Spain Lead Mexico at Half-Time
news.lede: Spain U-17 lead Mexico U-17 1-0 at half-time in their FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup Group F opener on Monday. Carolina Ferrera broke the deadlock in the 42nd minute, giving Spain a crucial advantage just before the interval. Spain dominated possession in the first half and created more scoring opportunities, forcing Mexico’s goalkeeper into several saves. Mexico, meanwhile, struggled to match Spain’s attacking intensity and will need a stronger second-half performance to get back into the contest.

news.title: Japan thrash Copper Princesses 5-0 in U17 Women’s World Cup opener
news.lede: Zambia’s Copper Princesses suffered a heavy 5-0 defeat to Japan in their opening Group D match at the FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. The Nadeshiko made a fast start at the Mohammed VI Football Complex Pitch 2 in Rabat, scoring twice inside the opening 13 minutes to put Zambia on the back foot. Nanami Kurita opened the scoring in the ninth minute, finishing from inside the box after Mei Hanashiro’s run and cut-back. Japan doubled their advantage four minutes later when Grace Phiri inadvertently turned the ball into her own net after Sayana Oshita met a corner from the right.
